questions.text: Which one of the following combinations is incorrect?
questions.solution:
Wheedle means to coax or flatter someone into doing something. It does not mean roundabout.

The other pairs are correct.

Answer: Wheedle - Roundabout

questions.text:
Based on the given statements, select the most appropriate option to solve the given question.

If two floors in a certain building are 9 feet apart, how many steps are there in a set of stairs that extends from the first floor to the second floor of the building?

Statements:

I. Each step is 3/4 foot high.
II. Each step is 1 foot wide.
questions.solution:
Number of steps = height / step height = 9 / (3/4) = 12, so statement I alone answers it.

The width of a step does not tell how many steps there are.

Answer: Statement I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not

options: Statements I alone is sufficient, but statement II alone is not sufficient.
Statements II alone is sufficient, but statement I alone is not sufficient.
Both statements together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.
Statements I and II together are not sufficient.?

questions.text: Given Set A=2,3,4,5 and Set B=11,12,13,14,15, two numbers are randomly selected, one from each set. What is the probability that the sum of the two numbers equals 16?
questions.solution:
Total pairs = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 5 = 20.

Sum 16: (2, 14), (3, 13), (4, 12), (5, 11) = 4 pairs

Probability = 4 / 20 = 0.2

Answer: 0.2

questions.text:
Which of the following options is the closest in meaning of the sentence below?

She enjoyed herself immensely at the party.
questions.solution:
"Enjoyed herself immensely" = had a very good time. "Terrific" means excellent here; terrible, horrible and terrifying are negative.

Answer: She had a terrific time at the party

questions.text: Didn't you buy ____ when you went shopping?
questions.solution:
"Any" is used in questions and negatives. "Paper" here is uncountable, so "a few" is wrong, and "no" makes a double negative.

Answer: any paper
